paths.description: Homepage and mandatory age-verification entry, representing first contact, consent, global navigation, and the content feed.
Video listing/navigation archetype; requested /video, which this regional experience redirects to the homepage feed.
Category/index navigation archetype; requested /categories, which this regional experience redirects to the homepage feed.
Representative media detail and playback page, including player, title, sharing/comment form, and related content.
Account authentication modal opened from the global Log In control; inspected labels, autocomplete, validation, SSO, and WebAuthn signals without submitting credentials.
Representative unknown URL used to inspect HTTP and user-facing recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The theme is fixed dark rather than driven by the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion evaluate probe reports document colorScheme "normal" with a black body under prefers-color-scheme: dark; the DOM/CSS contains no adaptive color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and express surface tokens with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme so browser chrome and site surfaces follow the user preference.

findings.summary: Player loading animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: On the video detail under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, two 1,500 ms dash animations remain running.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential animation in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and provide a static reduced-motion state.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use authored View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Five rendered-path probes found no authored transition rules or transition groups; route navigation is conventional abrupt MPA replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state continuity, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long feed has no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no container/scroll timeline rules and the long feed exposes static global chrome without progress or scroll-state feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky, scroll-state-aware chrome or a lightweight scroll progress/affordance where it helps users remain oriented.

findings.summary: Global overlays are custom div-based dialogs instead of native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows #js-ageDisclaimerModal is a div with role=alertdialog; probes found zero dialog, popover, or details elements across representative pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the blocking age/account flow and native popover/details for transient disclosures, preserving focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Advertising and repeated upgrade chrome compete heavily with primary content.
findings.evidence: HAR records 31 TrafficJunky image requests and 99 third-party requests; page text repeats “Remove Ads” throughout the feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated promotional chrome and defer ad slots so the media catalogue remains the visual and interaction priority.

findings.summary: The mandatory age gate is visibly clipped at 360 px.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot cuts off sentences, the law-enforcement link, and the right-hand “under 18” action. Layout metrics report no scroll because overflow is clipped rather than made reachable.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow the age gate to a single-column mobile layout, allow text wrapping, and stack both actions within the viewport.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport disables zoom and several essential text links have undersized targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports user-scalable=no/maximum-scale=1 on its mobile render. DOM measurements show age-gate links only 16–22 px high, below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit user scaling and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 44 CSS px without depending on the text glyph box.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently redirect to the homepage with no error or recovery explanation.
findings.evidence: HTTP probe shows an invented path returns 200 after redirect to /; the rendered probe contains ordinary homepage content and no 404/retry message.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status and a clear not-found state with search, home, and back recovery actions.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is poor and highly variable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP and TTI at 13.0 s (performance 65); the first-party trace measured LCP at 3.82 s, still above the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP image, remove lazy loading from it, add fetchpriority=high, and shorten render-blocking/network chains.

findings.summary: The load has a long render-blocking and dependency chain.
findings.evidence: HAR records 170 requests/4.36 MB and multiple VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets; Lighthouse estimates 620 ms render-blocking savings and flags an undiscoverable lazy LCP image.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, preload the LCP resource correctly, and improve cache/dependency ordering.

findings.summary: Substantial unused and legacy code ships on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 178 KiB unused JavaScript, roughly 74 KiB unused CSS, and 54 KiB legacy JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route/feature, remove legacy transforms for Baseline browsers, and load analytics/account code only when needed.

findings.summary: Several embedded and form controls lack robust accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails iframe title. The video detail probe finds an unlabeled caption textarea and submit button; the login modal also contains unnamed buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Title every iframe and give each field/control a persistent visible label or accurate accessible name.

findings.summary: Heading and accessible-name structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Homepage probes contain no H1 and begin with H3; Lighthouse flags the “Log in” control because its visible label does not match aria-label="User Icon".
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1 per template, logical heading levels, and accessible names that include visible control text.

findings.summary: The homepage throws an uncaught JavaScript exception.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading addEventListener) in setInstallButton at the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the install-button lookup or render the target before binding; add regression coverage for regional/page variants.

findings.summary: Several images lack intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports three images without dimensions; Lighthouse specifically identifies cookie/modal logo images without width and height.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio to every image so space is reserved before load.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and BFCache blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated unload handling, a deprecated Cast-control CSS technique, and four BFCache failure reasons including unload and no-store behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload listeners, use disableRemotePlayback, and eliminate avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: The homepage title is generic and rendered probes expose no meta description.
findings.evidence: Across homepage/listing probes the title is only “Pornhub” and description is null, providing little page-specific context.
findings.suggestedFix: Write unique descriptive titles and meta descriptions for homepage, listing, category, and detail templates.

findings.summary: Key links and crawler control files are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Probes count 30 missing/javascript href links; Lighthouse fails crawlable anchors. /robots.txt redirects to HTML and Lighthouse reports 4,071 parse errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real destination href values and serve a valid text/plain robots.txt at the requested URL.

findings.summary: Indexing signals conflict and detail pages canonicalize to the homepage.
findings.evidence: Representative pages emit noindex,nofollow; the video detail canonical is https://www.pornhub.com/; sitemap.xml returns 404; unknown routes redirect with 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Set page-specific canonicals, intentional robots directives, a valid sitemap, and correct 404 status behavior.

findings.summary: The video detail lacks rich-entity and share metadata.
findings.evidence: The video detail has zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags despite exposing a named video entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible title, thumbnail, duration, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Baseline XSS and cookie defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options; cookie evidence finds one non-Secure cookie and all seven cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and least-privilege Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The initial page has a large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence finds 12 third-party origins including GTM and DoubleClick. HAR attributes 99 requests and 2.01 MB to third parties before the primary content journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay optional analytics/ads until valid consent, reduce vendors and events, and batch/minimize telemetry.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no CSP/frame-ancestors policy, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; only X-Frame-Options and strong HSTS are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, nosniff, and Trusted Types where DOM XSS exposure warrants it.

findings.summary: The meaningful page becomes visually blank without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability finds only 31% rendered-word coverage; its crawler screenshot is entirely black while the JS-rendered screenshot shows the age gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the age gate and primary catalogue/content, then enhance interaction with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The login form does not expose required semantics or actionable empty-submit feedback.
findings.evidence: After opening login and submitting empty, email/password report required=false, aria-invalid is absent, and no visible role=alert/error text is returned.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, validate after interaction, connect field messages with aria-describedby, set aria-invalid, and announce a concise error summary.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes substantial bytes.
findings.evidence: Image evidence finds 33 images without srcset and 21 legacy formats; Lighthouse estimates 558 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive srcset/sizes variants, negotiate AVIF/WebP, and keep intrinsic dimensions and priority appropriate to viewport position.

findings.summary: The age-gated initial load performs disproportionate network work.
findings.evidence: Before entry, HAR records 170 requests and 4.36 MB including 39 scripts and 37 XHR/fetches; Lighthouse identifies large unused code payloads.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional catalogue, advertising, analytics, and account bundles behind user entry/consent and actual feature demand.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising dominates a large share of the initial transfer.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 2.01 MB and 99 requests to third parties, including 940 KB from TrafficJunky images and 303 KB from Google Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load below-fold ads, consolidate vendors, and stop background refresh when hidden.

findings.summary: The content platform exposes no structured agent capability and has malformed llms.txt guidance.
findings.evidence: Representative probes find no WebMCP/agentic surface; Lighthouse agentic browsing scores 67 and reports llms.txt missing its required H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid machine-readable discovery and, where safe, expose constrained WebMCP tools for search and content metadata rather than requiring scraping.
